To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we identified a homozygously nonsense mutation in CFAP57 in a patient with PCD, and we show that CFAP57, an uncharacterized protein, is required for the asymmetric loading of the inner dyneins onto the axonemal doublet microtubules.
a homozygotic nonsense mutation in CFAP57 results in a loss of a protein that is required for the asymmetric distribution of a subset of the inner dyneins, resulting in a PCD phenotype.
we have identified a homozygously mutated CFAP57 gene in a patient that causes a PCD phenotype, and that CFAP57 appears to be required for the assembly of the “g” and “d” inner arms in Chlamdomonas.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the genetic causes of primary ciliary dyskinnesia.
a mutation in a protein that is important in the formation of a subset of dynein arms, which are responsible for the beating of motile ciliary structures in the body.
a new disease gene, CFAP57, that is involved in the assembly of the inner dyneins of motile ciliary axonemes and sperm flagella.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the CFAP57 mutation causes PCD in humans and the fap57 mutation causes a defect in the assembly of the “g” and “d” inner arm dyneins in Chlamyomomas.
the CFAP57 gene is involved in PCD and that it is a new PCD gene, which has a role in inner dynein assembly.
the CFAP57 protein is required for the proper targeting of the “g” and “d” inner-dyneins to the axoneme and for the normal waveform and function of the axoneme in both Chlamydomonass and humans.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have identified the first CFAP57 mutation causing PCD and have shown that CFAP57 and FAP57 are orthologous proteins in human and Chlamydomnas that are important for the assembly of the inner dyneins.
CFAP57, an uncharacterized WD repeat-containing protein, is required for the asymmetric localization of a subset of the inner dyneins to the axoneme in Chlamyomdomas and in humans.
the CFAP57 protein, a member of the WD40 repeat protein family, is required for the assembly and/or stability of the inner dyneins in both human and Chlamydomonasspecies.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the identification of the causative gene for a PCD patient with a novel ciliary phenotype may be facilitated by a combination of bioinformatic analysis, cell culture, and a model organism.
CFAP57/FAP57 plays a critical role in the assembly of the inner dyneins, and that this is a highly conserved process across eukaryotic flagella.
the CFAP57 protein is required for the asymmetric localization of a subset of “g” inner arm dynein proteins.
